title: Every Line Has to Hold
tagline: A client presentation at nine, a construction site at two, and a structural problem that only shows up once the concrete's already poured.

wake_up.text: Today's the client presentation for the community center design — eight months of work distilled into forty-five minutes.

choices.text: Do one more full review of the presentation before leaving
Trust the work you've already put in

studio_arrival.text: The studio is quiet this early. Renderings printed, models on the table, everything ready except the nerves.

choices.text: Set up for the presentation

random_moment.text: The last hour before a big presentation has its own particular texture — a little different every time.

choices.text: A junior architect stops by just to say the design is beautiful
The plotter jams printing the final boards
Morning light through the studio windows hits the model just right

client_presentation.text: The client loves the design — until they ask to move the main entrance, a change that would ripple through half the structural plan.

choices.text: Explain honestly what the change would actually cost the design
Agree to explore it without raising concerns yet

site_visit_prep.text: The presentation wraps with a tentative yes on the design. Now it's time to check on the community center that's already under construction.

choices.text: Head to the construction site

site_arrival.text: The general contractor meets you at the gate, hard hat already in hand. "You're going to want to see this before we pour any more."

choices.text: See what he's talking about

structural_conflict.text: A load-bearing beam location conflicts with an HVAC run that was added after your drawings were finalized — nobody caught it until now, and the concrete for the next phase is scheduled to pour in six hours.

choices.text: Redesign the connection on-site, right now, with the contractor
Halt the pour and take it back to the studio to solve properly
Get the structural engineer on the phone before deciding anything
Approve the contractor's proposed workaround without a full review

conflict_outcome_onsite.text: Forty-five minutes of sketching on a plywood sheet with the contractor produces a clean solution that actually works. It's not how you pictured spending the afternoon, but the pour goes ahead on schedule.

choices.text: Confirm the revised plan

conflict_outcome_halt.text: The pour gets pushed two days. It costs the project real time and money, and the solution that comes out of a proper studio review is noticeably cleaner for the extra care.

choices.text: Send the revised drawings

conflict_outcome_engineer.text: The structural engineer talks through a fix over the phone in twenty minutes — a genuine collaboration under real time pressure, and it holds.

choices.text: Confirm the plan with the contractor

conflict_outcome_workaround.text: The contractor's workaround goes in fast — and it's not what you would have designed. Whether it holds up to code review later is now an open question hanging over the whole project.

choices.text: Continue the site walk

afternoon_site_walk.text: The rest of the site walk goes smoothly — until a subcontractor asks a question about a detail that was never fully resolved in the drawings.

choices.text: Stop and resolve the detail properly before moving on
Give a verbal answer and follow up with drawings later

studio_return.text: Back at the studio, the day's site notes need to become actual updated drawings before anyone else touches the project.

choices.text: Update the drawings tonight while everything's fresh
Leave detailed notes and update them tomorrow

end_shift.text: The studio empties out. Somewhere across town, concrete is curing around a decision you made this afternoon.

choices.text: Head home

triumphant.title: The Detail That Held
triumphant.blurb: Every call today was the right one, including the one made standing on plywood with a pencil. This is the project people point to.

steady_hand.title: Solid Work
steady_hand.blurb: No drama, no compromises that mattered — just careful, competent design decisions all day long.

ordinary_day.title: Another Day on Site
ordinary_day.blurb: A presentation, a site visit, a problem solved. Tomorrow there's another drawing set waiting.

burned_out.title: Running on Empty
burned_out.blurb: You made it through the day, but there's nothing left for tonight's drawings. This pace has a real cost.

written_up.title: Under Review
written_up.blurb: Something about today's on-site decision is going to come up in a code review. Nobody was hurt. The engineering still needs answers.
